text:
mira: noticed a perf regression on the canary this morning — short-sequence requests (<=12 tokens) latency jumped and some paged-KV hosts hit OOMs. anyone else seeing batch sizes ballooning?

jonathan: yea saw it in the kernel-canary metrics. selector started preferring FlashAttention-hybrid for small seqs after the kernel-swap last night. microbench looked good, but at runtime the setup/handshake cost plus prefetch pressure seems to be inflating queues -> larger batches for short seqs.

sam-ops: logs from host-43:
```
2026-03-18T08:12:09Z pagefault rate: 4.2x baseline
2026-03-18T08:12:12Z OOM kill: runtime-worker pid=8221
2026-03-18T08:12:12Z batch-formed: sum_tokens=4800, avg_seq=6, inflight_requests=220
```
we're seeing more KV page faults and prefetch thrash when FA-hybrid wins.

elaine: quick profiling note — KV residency fraction dropped from 94% -> 61% in the window. Prefetch threads queue length spiked and started evicting useful pages. I think token_budget target for small-seq class is too permissive (current=1024).

mira: proposal: for seq <= 8, reduce token_budget to 256 and lower batching timeout for small-seq queue to 8ms. also add a kernel override fastpath: prefer the lightweight attention kernel (no FA hybrid) under high-arrival-rate to avoid setup overhead. @tariq can you own the routing tweak?

tariq: yep. will push a canary with (a) token_budget=256 for small-seq slotting, (b) batch_timeout_ms=8 for that class, (c) kernel_override for seq<=8 when qps>180. deploying to canary pool now. ETA ~25m.

ci-bot: deploy started: canary/prefetch-overshoot-2067891234 -> hosts [host-41, host-42, host-43]

jonathan: after ~10m of canary traffic: p50 for short seqs dropped from 62ms -> 22ms and throughput stabilized. pagefault-rate back to near-baseline. nice.

sam-ops: one remaining spike on host-42: root cause appears to be selector flip-flop when concurrent kernel swaps coincide with sudden QPS surges. selector currently swaps without cooldown; causes microthundering.

elaine: agree — follow-ups:
- add 100ms cooldown per worker after kernel_swap decision
- cap prefetch concurrency to 4 threads per worker
- add a simple metric: kernel_swap_rate per minute to alert on thrash
I'll open PRs for those.

mira: sounds good. if this had caused a customer outage we'd postmortem; since canary recovered we do follow-ups and close. thanks all :thumbsup:

ci-bot: canary completed successfully, promoting to eu-west-1.
